subproblem.title: Simon 6.2.30–6.2.32 and 6.3.10: the cone over a compactly supported integer multiplicity cycle is an integer multiplicity filling
subproblem.statement: Let n, P ∈ ℕ and let S ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (a GeometricCurrentOn univ (n + 1) on ℝ^P = Euclid P) be an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity S: S = τ(M, θ, ξ) for an IMRep in ℝ^P) with spt S compact and ∂S = 0 (S.boundary = 0). Then there is an integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{n+2}(ℝ^P) with spt R compact and ∂R = S (R.boundary = S). (R is Simon's cone 0 ⨯ S = h_#([[(0,1)]] × S), h(t, x) = tx.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n P : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsCompact S.support → S.boundary = 0 → ∃ R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 2), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsCompact R.support ∧ R.boundary = S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, 2.25–2.32 and 3.9–3.10 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 441–551 and 857–865). This is the book's claim “𝓘_S ≠ ∅ (e.g. 0 ⨯ S ∈ 𝓘_S)” in the proof of Simon 7.2.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 103–104), which is Step 1 of the supplied proof. Simon defines the cone 0 ⨯ S := h_#([[(0,1)]] × S), h(t, x) = tx (2.30), obtains ∂(0 ⨯ S) = S − 0 ⨯ ∂S from the homotopy formula 2.25 (2.31), and obtains integrality from 3.9 (3.10). The printed 3.9 rests on C¹ submanifold covers and the area formula on them (Ch. 3), which the pinned library does not provide. The proof below follows the same construction with two changes. (a) h_#([[(0,1)]] × ·) is written at the level of forms through the Poincaré homotopy operator K (Part B). (b) Integrality is proved through integral Lipschitz parametrizations (Parts C–G). It uses only Mathlib, the checked SimonGMT results cited by name (Lipschitz area formula, Rademacher's theorem, Simon's density theorem 3.6) and the sibling support lemma. Every auxiliary fact is proved below as a numbered part; no further named lemma is needed.

Sibling lemma used: support_vanishing (accepted as dtc_vanish_off_support). If X ∈ 𝒟_p(U) and γ ∈ 𝒟^p(U) with tsupport γ ∩ spt X = ∅, then X(γ) = 0.

Notation.
- k := n + 1 ≥ 1 is the dimension of S, so R will have dimension k + 1 = n + 2.
- All currents are on U = ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ). A test p-form is a C^∞ compactly supported map ℝ^P → Λ^p(ℝ^P), where Λ^p(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) p is the space of continuous alternating p-linear maps.
- |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a p-covector (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm: |α|² = Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_p})² over strictly increasing I), and |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|.
- dx^I is the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J. The dx^I form a basis of Λ^p(ℝ^P), and |dx^I| = 1.
- The exterior derivative is SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv: dβ(y)(w_0, …, w_p) = Σ_{i=0}^p (−1)^i Dβ(y)[w_i](w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_p). Here Dβ(y)[w] is the derivative of the covector-valued map β at y in direction w (exteriorDerivative_apply).
- H^p := μHE[p]. On ℝ^p it is Lebesgue measure L^p (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and it equals Simon's H^p (library Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
- B_r(y) and B̄_r(y) are the open and closed balls, and η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (library blowUpMap).
- Let F : ℝ^p → ℝ^P and u ∈ ℝ^p.
  - DF(u) := fderiv ℝ F u, the zero map where F is not differentiable.
  - ∂F(u) := (DF(u)e_1, …, DF(u)e_p).
  - JF(u) := J(∂F(u)), where J(v_1, …, v_p) := (det[v_a·v_b]_{a,b})^{1/2} for v_1, …, v_p ∈ ℝ^P.
- For linear D put J(D) := J(De_1, …, De_p). Then J(D) = (det(D^*D))^{1/2} = normDet D, which is the library areaJacobianAt (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp; the matrix of D^*D in the standard basis is the Gram matrix). Moreover J(D) > 0 iff D is injective.
- A parametrization of dimension p of X ∈ 𝒟_p(ℝ^P) is a family (F_j, A_j, g_j)_{j∈ℕ}, with F_j : ℝ^p → ℝ^P Lipschitz, A_j ⊆ ℝ^p Borel and g_j : ℝ^p → ℤ measurable, such that
  (LF) Σ_j ∫_{A_j ∩ F_j^{-1}(C)} |g_j| JF_j dL^p < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ ℝ^P, and
  (REP) X(γ) = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} g_j(u) γ(F_j(u))(∂F_j(u)) du for every test p-form γ.

PART A. Linear algebra.
A1 (pull-back norm; Simon 6.1, used in 6.2.27). Let L : ℝ^q → ℝ^P be linear and α ∈ Λ^p(ℝ^P), and put L^#α := α(L·, …, L·). Then |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^p|α|. Proof.
 (a) Let V_1, …, V_p be Euclidean spaces with orthonormal bases (b^{(r)}_i) and γ a p-linear map on V_1 × ⋯ × V_p. Put HS(γ) := Σ_{i_1,…,i_p} γ(b^{(1)}_{i_1}, …, b^{(p)}_{i_p})², summing over all index tuples (HS(γ) = γ()² if p = 0). On ℝ^d we use the standard basis.
 (b) For an alternating p-linear β on ℝ^d, HS(β) = p!|β|². Tuples with a repeated index contribute 0. Each tuple of distinct indices is I∘σ for a unique increasing I and permutation σ, and β(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)β(e_I).
 (c) Suppose γ' arises from γ by inserting a linear A : V' → V_r into slot r. Then HS(γ') ≤ ‖A‖²HS(γ). Fix the other indices. Then v ↦ γ(…, v, …) equals ⟨a, v⟩ for some a ∈ V_r, so Σ_i γ(…, b^{(r)}_i, …)² = |a|² and Σ_j γ(…, Ab'_j, …)² = |Aᵀa|² ≤ ‖A‖²|a|². Now sum over the other indices.
 (d) Inserting L into all p slots gives HS(L^#α) ≤ ‖L‖^{2p}HS(α). By (b), p!|L^#α|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2p}p!|α|². Take square roots.
A2 (Gram–Schmidt). Let v_1, …, v_p ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^p(ℝ^P).
 - If the v_i are linearly dependent, then α(v) = 0 and J(v) = 0.
 - Otherwise let τ_1, …, τ_p be their Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization, so v_j = Σ_i R_{ij}τ_i with R upper triangular with positive diagonal. Then [v_a·v_b] = RᵀR, so J(v) = det R > 0, and α(v) = det(R)α(τ) = J(v)α(τ) by multilinearity and alternation.
 - Let ι : ℝ^p → ℝ^P be the linear isometry e_i ↦ τ_i. The p-covector ι^#α on ℝ^p has the single increasing index tuple (1, …, p), so |α(τ)| = |ι^#α| ≤ |α| by A1.
 Hence:
 (A2a) |α(v)| ≤ |α|J(v) always.
 (A2b) For independent v, ξ_v(α) := α(v)/J(v) = α(τ) is a unit orientation of span(v) in the sense of IsUnitOrientationOf (orthonormal basis τ, sign +).
 For injective linear D write ξ_D := ξ_{(De_1, …, De_p)}, and put ξ_D := 0 for non-injective D. The map D ↦ ξ_D is Borel: it is continuous on the open set of injective D, since ξ_D(α) = α(De_1, …, De_p)/J(D) with J continuous and positive there, and constant on the closed complement.
A3 (unit orientations). Let ξ and ξ' be unit orientations of one p-dimensional subspace Q: ξ(α) = εα(τ) and ξ'(α) = ε'α(τ'), with orthonormal bases τ, τ' of Q and ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1}.
 (a) ξ' = ±ξ. Indeed τ'_i = Σ_l B_{il}τ_l with B orthogonal, so α(τ') = det(B)α(τ) and det B = ±1.
 (b) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, by A2a with v = τ and J(τ) = 1.
 (c) ξ(dx^I) ≠ 0 for some increasing I. Indeed β(w_1, …, w_p) := det[τ_i·w_j] is an alternating p-form with β(τ) = 1, so ξ(β) = ±1, while β = Σ_I β(e_I)dx^I.
A4 (cone Jacobian). Let a, w_1, …, w_p ∈ ℝ^P and s ≥ 0.
 - J(a, sw_1, …, sw_p) = s^p J(a, w_1, …, w_p), by homogeneity of the Gram determinant.
 - J(a, w_1, …, w_p) ≤ |a| J(w_1, …, w_p). If the w_i are dependent, both sides vanish. Otherwise, permuting the vectors conjugates the Gram matrix by a permutation matrix, so J(a, w) = J(w, a). By Gram–Schmidt in the order w_1, …, w_p, a, the Gram determinant is the product of the squared lengths of the successive orthogonal components. Hence J(w, a)² = J(w)²|a − π_W a|² ≤ J(w)²|a|², where W := span(w).

PART B. The cone current R, its boundary and its support.
B1 (homotopy operator). For p ≥ 1 and a C^∞ p-form β on ℝ^P put
 (K_pβ)(x)(v_1, …, v_{p−1}) := ∫_0^1 t^{p−1} β(tx)(x, v_1, …, v_{p−1}) dt.
 This is a Bochner integral in the finite-dimensional space Λ^{p−1}(ℝ^P); the integrand is alternating in v because β(tx) is. The map (t, x) ↦ t^{p−1}β(tx)(x, ·) is C^∞ on ℝ × ℝ^P and t ranges over the compact interval [0, 1]. Hence K_pβ is C^∞, and its x-derivatives of every order are obtained by differentiating under the integral sign. If β(tx) = 0 for all t ∈ [0, 1], then (K_pβ)(x) = 0.
B2 (homotopy formula; Simon 2.25 for h(t, x) = tx, from f = 0 to g = id). For p ≥ 1 and every C^∞ p-form β: β = d(K_pβ) + K_{p+1}(dβ). Proof.
 - Fix x and v_1, …, v_p. For each i, differentiate y ↦ (K_pβ)(y)(v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p) at x in direction v_i under the integral sign. This gives ∫_0^1 t^{p−1}[t Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p) + β(tx)(v_i, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p)] dt, and β(tx)(v_i, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p) = (−1)^{i−1}β(tx)(v_1, …, v_p).
 - By the formula for d (with w_0 = v_1, …, w_{p−1} = v_p),
  d(K_pβ)(x)(v) = Σ_{i=1}^p (−1)^{i−1} D_{v_i}[(K_pβ)(·)(…v̂_i…)](x) = ∫_0^1 [p t^{p−1}β(tx)(v) + t^p Σ_{i=1}^p (−1)^{i−1} Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p)] dt.
 - By the formula for d with w_0 = x and w_i = v_i,
  K_{p+1}(dβ)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^p[Dβ(tx)[x](v) + Σ_{i=1}^p (−1)^i Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_p)] dt.
 - Adding, the two sums cancel. So d(K_pβ)(x)(v) + K_{p+1}(dβ)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 φ'(t) dt with φ(t) := t^pβ(tx)(v), since φ'(t) = pt^{p−1}β(tx)(v) + t^pDβ(tx)[x](v). This equals φ(1) − φ(0) = β(x)(v), because p ≥ 1.
B3 (definition; Simon 2.30). spt S is compact. If spt S = ∅ put V := ∅ and ζ := 0. Otherwise choose δ > 0 and apply Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff to the closed set cthickening δ (spt S) inside the bounded open set thickening (2δ) (spt S). This gives a C^∞ ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with compact tsupport and ζ = 1 on the open set V := thickening δ (spt S) ⊇ spt S. For a test (k+1)-form ω, ζK_{k+1}ω is C^∞ with tsupport in the compact set tsupport ζ, hence a test k-form. Define R(ω) := S(ζK_{k+1}ω). R is ℝ-linear.
B4 (R is a current).
 - Let ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges): a compact K₁ contains every tsupport ω_j, and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K₁. Each ω_j vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K₁, so all its derivatives vanish there. Hence ε_{j,a} := sup_{y∈ℝ^P}‖D^aω_j(y)‖ → 0 for every a.
 - Write (K_{k+1}ω_j)(x) = ∫_0^1 t^k Π(ω_j(tx), x) dt with the continuous bilinear map Π(α, x) := α(x, ·). By the Leibniz rule (the second argument x has derivative the identity and vanishing higher derivatives) and D^b_x[ω_j(tx)] = t^b(D^bω_j)(tx), we get ‖D^a(K_{k+1}ω_j)(x)‖ ≤ C_a(1 + |x|) max_{b≤a} ε_{j,b}.
 - By the Leibniz rule for ζ·K_{k+1}ω_j, every iterated derivative of ζK_{k+1}ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on the compact set tsupport ζ, which contains all their supports. So ζK_{k+1}ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, and R(ω_j) = S(ζK_{k+1}ω_j) → 0 by the continuity of S.
 - Thus R ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_{n+2}(ℝ^P), i.e. R is a GeometricCurrentOn univ (n + 2).
B5 (∂R = S; Simon 2.31 with ∂S = 0). Let ω be a test k-form. Since dω is a test (k+1)-form, ∂R(ω) = R(dω) = S(ζK_{k+1}(dω)). By B2 with p = k ≥ 1, K_{k+1}(dω) = ω − d(K_kω). Hence ∂R(ω) = S(ζω) − S(ζ d(K_kω)).
 (a) ζω − ω vanishes on the open set V ⊇ spt S, so tsupport(ζω − ω) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ V is disjoint from spt S. Support_vanishing and linearity give S(ζω) = S(ω).
 (b) ζK_kω is a test (k−1)-form (C^∞, with tsupport ⊆ tsupport ζ). On V, ζ = 1 near every point, and the exterior derivative at a point depends only on the form near that point. So the test k-forms ζ d(K_kω) and d(ζK_kω) agree on V, and their difference has tsupport disjoint from spt S. By support_vanishing, S(ζ d(K_kω)) = S(d(ζK_kω)) = (∂S)(ζK_kω) = 0. The last step holds because ∂S = 0: S.boundary is the current of degree k − 1 = n with (∂S)(γ) = S(dγ).
 Hence ∂R(ω) = S(ω) for every test k-form ω, i.e. R.boundary = S.
B6 (spt R compact; Simon: spt(0 ⨯ S) ⊆ {tx}). C₀ := {tx : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt S} is compact, as the continuous image of [0, 1] × spt S.
 - Let ω be a test (k+1)-form with tsupport ω ∩ C₀ = ∅. The set W := {x : tx ∉ tsupport ω for all t ∈ [0, 1]} is open. Its complement is the image of the closed set {(t, x) ∈ [0, 1] × ℝ^P : tx ∈ tsupport ω} under the projection [0, 1] × ℝ^P → ℝ^P, which is a closed map because [0, 1] is compact.
 - W ⊇ spt S, and (K_{k+1}ω)(x) = 0 for x ∈ W (B1). So ζK_{k+1}ω vanishes on W, and its tsupport lies in ℝ^P ∖ W, which is disjoint from spt S. Hence R(ω) = 0 by support_vanishing.
 - Now let x ∉ C₀ and choose r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x) ∩ C₀ = ∅ (C₀ is closed; take r = 1 if C₀ = ∅). The ball B_r(x) is open with compact closure. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(x) satisfies tsupport ω ∩ C₀ = ∅, hence R(ω) = 0. So B_r(x) lies in the zero region of R, and x ∉ spt R.
 - Thus spt R ⊆ C₀. Since spt R = ℝ^P ∖ (zero region) is closed, spt R is compact.
It remains to show that R is integer multiplicity.

PART C. Pieces, area formula, null sets and density (p ≥ 1 throughout).
C1 (bi-Lipschitz pieces). Let F : ℝ^p → ℝ^P be Lipschitz, and let G be a Borel subset of the regular set G_F := {u : F differentiable at u and DF(u) injective}. (G_F is Borel by library Chapter02.measurableSet_areaRegularSet.) Then G = ⋃_i T_i for pairwise disjoint Borel T_i (i ∈ ℕ), with constants c_i > 0 such that |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ c_i|v − w| for v, w ∈ T_i. Proof.
 - For injective linear A : ℝ^p → ℝ^P choose N_A ≥ 1 with |v| ≤ N_A|Av| for all v (A is antilipschitz), and put δ(A) := 1/(2N_A). Put δ(A) := 1 for non-injective A.
 - Apply Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean) to F, G, f' := fderiv ℝ F and r := δ; F has derivative DF(u) within G at each u ∈ G. It yields pairwise disjoint Borel t_i with G ⊆ ⋃t_i and continuous linear A_i with |F(v) − F(w) − A_i(v − w)| ≤ δ(A_i)|v − w| for v, w ∈ G ∩ t_i. If G ≠ ∅, then A_i = DF(x_i) for some x_i ∈ G, hence A_i is injective.
 - With T_i := G ∩ t_i and c_i := 1/(2N_{A_i}): |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ |A_i(v − w)| − δ(A_i)|v − w| ≥ c_i|v − w|.
C2 (one piece). Let F be Λ_F-Lipschitz and T ⊆ G_F a Borel set with |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ c|v − w| on T, where c > 0. Every piece produced by C1 qualifies.
 (a) T ∩ F^{-1}(B) is bounded for bounded B.
 (b) F(B) is Borel for Borel B ⊆ T (Lusin–Souslin, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). The inverse ψ : F(T) → T is Borel, since F restricted to T is a measurable embedding.
 (c) Area formula: for Borel B ⊆ T and Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫_{F(B)} g dH^p = ∫_B JF(v) g(F(v)) dv. This is library Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (F globally Lipschitz, B measurable, F injective on B). Splitting g = g⁺ − g⁻, the same holds for real Borel g integrable on F(B). Moreover 0 < JF(v) ≤ Λ_F^p for v ∈ T. Positivity holds because DF(v) is injective (T ⊆ G_F). The upper bound holds because JF(v)² = det(DF(v)^*DF(v)) is a product of p eigenvalues, each ≤ ‖DF(v)‖² ≤ Λ_F².
 (d) If H^p(Z) = 0 then L^p(T ∩ F^{-1}(Z)) = 0. Choose a Borel Z' ⊇ Z with H^p(Z') = 0. By (c), ∫_T JF·1_{Z'}∘F = H^p(F(T) ∩ Z') = 0, and JF > 0 on T.
 (e) For every Λ_F-Lipschitz F and every Z ⊆ ℝ^p, H^p(F(Z)) ≤ Λ_F^p L^p(Z) (library euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), so F maps L^p-null sets to H^p-null sets. Also H^p(F(ℝ^p ∖ G_F)) = 0 (library Chapter02.area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero).
 (f) H^p(F(T) ∩ C) ≤ Λ_F^p L^p(T ∩ F^{-1}(C)) < ∞ for compact C, by (a) and (e).
C3 (density zero; Simon 3.6). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^p(A ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C. Then for H^p-a.e. y ∉ A, r^{-p}H^p(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) → 0 as r ↓ 0. Proof.
 - For R ∈ ℕ, A_R := A ∩ B_R(0) is Borel with H^p(A_R) < ∞.
 - Apply Simon's Theorem 3.6 in the library (Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside) to the outer measure of H^p and the Carathéodory measurable set A_R of finite measure. That outer measure is Borel regular (Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular), and the theorem's “a.e.” refers to simonHausdorffMeasureReal p = H^p (Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). It gives, for H^p-a.e. y ∉ A_R, limsup_{r↓0} H^p(A_R ∩ B̄_r(y))/(ω_p r^p) = 0, where ω_p = realUnitBallVolume p ∈ (0, ∞).
 - Let Z be the union over R of the exceptional null sets. If y ∉ A ∪ Z, choose R > |y| + 1. For 0 < r < 1, A ∩ B̄_r(y) = A_R ∩ B̄_r(y) and y ∉ A_R, so r^{-p}H^p(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) → 0.
C4 (comparison of blow-ups). Let A, B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^p(A ∩ C) < ∞ and H^p(B ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C.
 (a) Let y ∈ ℝ^P, and suppose r^{-p}H^p((A ∖ B) ∩ B̄_r(y)) → 0 and r^{-p}H^p((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_r(y)) → 0. Then ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^p − ∫_{η_{y,r}(B)} f dH^p → 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P); hence A has approximate tangent space Q at y iff B has.
  - η_{y,r} is injective: a homothety of ratio 1/r followed by a translation. So η_{y,r}(X) is Borel for Borel X, and H^p(η_{y,r}(X)) = r^{-p}H^p(X) (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image and translation invariance).
  - If spt f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0), the difference is at most ‖f‖_∞[H^p(η_{y,r}(A ∖ B) ∩ B_{R₀}(0)) + H^p(η_{y,r}(B ∖ A) ∩ B_{R₀}(0))] ≤ ‖f‖_∞r^{-p}[H^p((A ∖ B) ∩ B̄_{rR₀}(y)) + H^p((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{rR₀}(y))] → 0. All the integrals are finite, since f is bounded with compact support.
 (b) If H^p(A △ B) = 0, the blow-up integrals coincide for every r. So A and B have the same approximate tangent spaces at every point.
 (c) By C3 applied to A ∖ B and to B ∖ A, the hypothesis of (a) holds at H^p-a.e. y ∈ A ∩ B.

PART D. Approximate tangent planes along Lipschitz maps.
Claim D. Let p ≥ 1, let F : ℝ^p → ℝ^P be Λ_F-Lipschitz, and let Y ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^p(Y ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C. Then for L^p-a.e. u the following holds: if F(u) ∈ Y, F is differentiable at u and DF(u) is injective, then Y has approximate tangent space DF(u)(ℝ^p) at F(u), i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt p Y (F u) (range DF(u)).
D1 (reduction to one piece). By C1 with G = G_F, G_F = ⋃_i T_i. The u in question lie in G_F, and a countable union of null sets is null. So it suffices to prove the claim for a.e. u ∈ T := T_i, with constant c. Put N := F(T); it is Borel with H^p(N ∩ C) < ∞ for compact C, by C2(b),(f).
D2 (bad set). By C4(c) with A = Y and B = N, there is an H^p-null set Z_bad such that the hypothesis of C4(a) for (Y, N) holds at every y ∈ (Y ∩ N) ∖ Z_bad. By C2(d), U_bad := T ∩ F^{-1}(Z_bad) is L^p-null.
D3 (good points). Call u ∈ T ∩ F^{-1}(Y) good if
 (i) u ∉ U_bad;
 (ii) L^p(B_ρ(u) ∖ T)/L^p(B_ρ(u)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0;
 (iii) ρ^{-p}∫_{B_ρ(u)} |1_T(v)JF(v) − JF(u)| dv → 0.
 Conditions (ii) and (iii) hold at L^p-a.e. u ∈ T by the Lebesgue density and differentiation theorems: Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div and VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the Besicovitch Vitali family of L^p, applied to the bounded Borel function 1_T·JF. (JF is Borel because fderiv ℝ F is, by Mathlib measurable_fderiv; balls and their closures differ by null sets.) So L^p-a.e. u ∈ T ∩ F^{-1}(Y) is good. Fix a good u and put y := F(u) ∈ Y ∩ N, D := DF(u) and Q := D(ℝ^p); finrank Q = p.
D4 (|Dw| ≥ c|w|). Let w ≠ 0 and ε ∈ (0, 1).
 - For small ρ > 0 the ball B_{ερ|w|}(u + ρw) meets T. Otherwise B_{2ρ|w|}(u) ∖ T contains it, a fixed fraction (ε/2)^p of L^p(B_{2ρ|w|}(u)), contradicting (ii) for arbitrarily small ρ. Pick v_ρ ∈ T in that ball.
 - By the piece property, |F(v_ρ) − F(u)| ≥ c|v_ρ − u| ≥ cρ|w|(1 − ε). By differentiability, F(v_ρ) − F(u) = D(v_ρ − u) + o(ρ), and |D(v_ρ − u) − ρDw| ≤ ‖D‖ερ|w|.
 - Hence ρ|Dw| ≥ cρ|w|(1 − ε) − ‖D‖ερ|w| − o(ρ). Divide by ρ, let ρ ↓ 0, then let ε ↓ 0.
D5 (blow-up of N). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0).
 - For Borel X, H^p(N ∩ η_{y,r}^{-1}(X)) = r^pH^p(η_{y,r}(N) ∩ X), by the scaling identity in C4(a). So ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} f dH^p = r^{-p}∫_N f∘η_{y,r} dH^p.
 - By C2(c) (f∘η_{y,r} is bounded and vanishes off a compact set, on which H^p⌞N is finite) and the substitution v = u + rw:
  ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} f dH^p = r^{-p}∫_T f((F(v) − y)/r) JF(v) dv = ∫_{(T−u)/r} f(Φ_r(w)) JF(u + rw) dw, where Φ_r(w) := (F(u + rw) − F(u))/r.
 - If u + rw ∈ T then |Φ_r(w)| ≥ c|w|. So the integrand vanishes unless |w| < R₁ := R₀/c, and
  ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} f dH^p = ∫_{B_{R₁}(0)} 1_T(u + rw) JF(u + rw) f(Φ_r(w)) dw.
 - As r ↓ 0, sup_{|w|≤R₁}|Φ_r(w) − Dw| → 0 by Fréchet differentiability, so sup_{|w|≤R₁}|f(Φ_r(w)) − f(Dw)| → 0 by uniform continuity of f. Also ∫_{B_{R₁}(0)}|1_T(u + rw)JF(u + rw) − JF(u)| dw = r^{-p}∫_{B_{rR₁}(u)}|1_TJF − JF(u)| → 0 by (iii).
 - Since |f| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ and 0 ≤ 1_TJF ≤ Λ_F^p,
  ∫_{η_{y,r}(N)} f dH^p → JF(u)∫_{B_{R₁}(0)} f(Dw) dw = J(D)∫_{ℝ^p} f(Dw) dw = ∫_Q f dH^p.
  The first equality holds because f(Dw) = 0 for |w| ≥ R₁ (D4 gives |Dw| ≥ cR₁ = R₀). The second is the linear area formula: library Chapter02.weighted_linear_area_formula for the injective linear D and the set ℝ^p, applied to f⁺ and f⁻, with normDet D = J(D) and H^p = L^p on ℝ^p.
D6 (blow-up of Y; conclusion). y ∈ (Y ∩ N) ∖ Z_bad by (i), so C4(a) gives ∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} f dH^p → ∫_Q f dH^p for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Thus Y has approximate tangent space Q = DF(u)(ℝ^p) at F(u). The exceptional u of the claim lie in the union over the pieces T_i of the non-good points of T_i ∩ F^{-1}(Y), a countable union of L^p-null sets. ∎(Claim D)

PART E. A parametrization of S with images in spt S.
Let (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of S (IsIntegerMultiplicity S). Thus:
 - M ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel and countably k-rectifiable;
 - θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable, θ ≥ 1 on M, and ∫_{M∩C} θ dH^k < ∞ for compact C (hence H^k(M ∩ C) < ∞);
 - ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) is AE-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M;
 - for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M some Q_x satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q_x, and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q_x;
 - S(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dH^k for every test k-form γ, where ξ(γ) means x ↦ ξ(x)(γ(x)).
Replace ξ by a Borel (strongly measurable) map equal to it H^k⌞M-a.e. (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). This changes neither the representation nor the a.e. orientation property, so we keep the name ξ. By A3(b), |θξ(γ)| ≤ θ|γ|_∞1_{tsupport γ} H^k-a.e. on M, and the right side is integrable on M.
E1 (H^k(M ∖ spt S) = 0).
 - G₀ := ℝ^P ∖ spt S is the zero region of S, an open set. By support_vanishing, S(γ) = 0 for every test k-form γ with tsupport γ ⊆ G₀.
 - For increasing I let a_I := θ ξ(dx^I), with dx^I the constant coordinate form. Put ν := H^k⌞M. Then a_I is locally ν-integrable, since |a_I| ≤ θ ν-a.e. (A3(b)).
 - Let φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with tsupport φ ⊆ G₀. Then γ := φ dx^I is a test k-form with tsupport γ ⊆ G₀, so 0 = S(γ) = ∫ φ a_I dν. By Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, a_I = 0 ν-a.e. on G₀, for every I.
 - But at ν-a.e. x ∈ M, θ(x) ≥ 1 and ξ(x)(dx^I) ≠ 0 for some I (A3(c)). Hence ν(G₀) = H^k(M ∖ spt S) = 0.
E2 (pieces with disjoint images).
 - By CountablyRectifiable k M there are an H^k-null set M₀ and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^k).
 - The sets E_j := {u ∈ G_{F_j} : F_j(u) ∈ M ∩ spt S} are Borel, since spt S is closed. By C1 each E_j is a disjoint union of Borel pieces. Enumerate all pieces of all E_j as (Φ_l, P_l)_{l∈ℕ}, where Φ_l is the F_j of its E_j.
 - Disjointify the images: P'_l := P_l ∖ Φ_l^{-1}(⋃_{l'<l} Φ_{l'}(P_{l'})), which is Borel by C2(b). The Borel sets Φ_l(P'_l) are pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_l Φ_l(P'_l) = ⋃_l Φ_l(P_l) =: N ⊆ M ∩ spt S.
 - (M ∩ spt S) ∖ N ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^k ∖ G_{F_j}), which is H^k-null by C2(e). With E1, H^k(M ∖ N) = 0.
E3 (orientations and weights).
 - For u ∈ P'_l, DΦ_l(u) is injective. Let ξ_l(u) := ξ_{DΦ_l(u)} (A2b), a unit orientation of DΦ_l(u)(ℝ^k).
 - By Claim D for (Φ_l, Y := M), for L^k-a.e. u ∈ P'_l the set M has approximate tangent space DΦ_l(u)(ℝ^k) at Φ_l(u).
 - The set Y₁ of x ∈ M where the IMRep orientation property fails is H^k-null, so Φ_l^{-1}(Y₁) ∩ P'_l is L^k-null by C2(d).
 - For the remaining u ∈ P'_l, uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (library Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) gives Q_{Φ_l(u)} = DΦ_l(u)(ℝ^k). Then A3(a) gives ξ(Φ_l(u)) = ε_l(u)ξ_l(u) with ε_l(u) ∈ {1, −1}.
 - Let A_l ⊆ P'_l be a Borel set of full measure on which this holds. ε_l is Borel on A_l: ε_l(u) = 1 iff ‖ξ(Φ_l u) − ξ_l(u)‖ < ‖ξ(Φ_l u) + ξ_l(u)‖, for any norm on the finite-dimensional MultiVector P k (note ξ(Φ_l u) = ±ξ_l(u) ≠ 0). The maps u ↦ ξ(Φ_l u) and u ↦ ξ_l(u) are Borel, since ξ is Borel, Φ_l is continuous, fderiv ℝ Φ_l is Borel, and A2b applies.
 - Put g_l(u) := ε_l(u)θ(Φ_l(u)) ∈ ℤ for u ∈ A_l, and g_l := 0 elsewhere (measurable).
E4 (REP and LF).
 - Let γ be a test k-form. The argument uses:
  - H^k(M ∖ N) = 0;
  - countable additivity of the integral over the disjoint Borel sets Φ_l(P'_l), since the integrand is integrable;
  - C2(c) on each piece, and H^k(Φ_l(P'_l ∖ A_l)) = 0 by C2(e);
  - ξ(Φ_l u)(α)JΦ_l(u) = ε_l(u)ξ_l(u)(α)JΦ_l(u) = ε_l(u)α(∂Φ_l(u)) on A_l, by A2b.
 It gives
  S(γ) = ∫_N θξ(γ) dH^k = Σ_l ∫_{Φ_l(A_l)} θξ(γ) dH^k = Σ_l ∫_{A_l} θ(Φ_l u) ξ(Φ_l u)(γ(Φ_l u)) JΦ_l(u) du = Σ_l ∫_{A_l} g_l(u) γ(Φ_l(u))(∂Φ_l(u)) du.
 - For compact C, C2(c) with g = θ1_C and disjointness of the images give Σ_l ∫_{A_l ∩ Φ_l^{-1}(C)} |g_l| JΦ_l = Σ_l ∫_{Φ_l(A_l) ∩ C} θ dH^k ≤ ∫_{M∩C} θ dH^k < ∞.
 - Re-index the Φ_l, A_l, g_l as F_j, A_j, g_j. These are Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, Borel sets A_j ⊆ ℝ^k and measurable g_j : ℝ^k → ℤ (j ∈ ℕ) such that F_j is differentiable at every point of A_j, F_j(A_j) ⊆ spt S, and (LF) and (REP) hold for S.

PART F. A parametrization of R.
F1. Choose ρ > 0 with spt S ⊆ B_ρ(0). Let r_ρ be the 1-Lipschitz radial retraction onto B̄_ρ(0): r_ρ(y) = y for |y| ≤ ρ and ρy/|y| otherwise. F̂_j := r_ρ∘F_j is Lipschitz with |F̂_j| ≤ ρ, and F̂_j = F_j on the open set F_j^{-1}(B_ρ(0)) ⊇ A_j. Hence for u ∈ A_j, F̂_j is differentiable at u with DF̂_j(u) = DF_j(u) and F̂_j(u) = F_j(u).
F2. Identify ℝ^{k+1} = Euclid (k+1) with ℝ × ℝ^k by w = (w_0, w_1, …, w_k) ↦ (s, u) := (w_0, (w_1, …, w_k)). This linear bijection carries Lebesgue measure to the product of the Lebesgue measures (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp and MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0), and the standard basis vector e_0 of ℝ^{k+1} is the s-direction.
 - Let σ(s) := min(max(s, 0), 1) and G_j(s, u) := σ(s)F̂_j(u). Then G_j : ℝ^{k+1} → ℝ^P is Lipschitz, since |G_j(s,u) − G_j(s',u')| ≤ ρ|s − s'| + Lip(F_j)|u − u'|.
 - Put Ã_j := (0, 1) × A_j (Borel) and g̃_j(s, u) := g_j(u) (measurable, ℤ-valued).
F3. Let (s, u) ∈ Ã_j.
 - G_j(s', u') = s'F̂_j(u') near (s, u). So G_j is differentiable at (s, u), with DG_j(s,u)e_0 = F_j(u) and DG_j(s,u)e_i = sDF_j(u)e_i for 1 ≤ i ≤ k; that is, ∂G_j(s, u) = (F_j(u), s∂F_j(u)).
 - For a test (k+1)-form ω, multilinearity gives ω(G_j(s,u))(∂G_j(s,u)) = s^kω(sF_j(u))(F_j(u), ∂F_j(u)). Hence (K_{k+1}ω)(F_j(u))(∂F_j(u)) = ∫_0^1 ω(G_j(s,u))(∂G_j(s,u)) ds.
 - By A4, JG_j(s,u) = s^kJ(F_j(u), ∂F_j(u)) ≤ s^k|F_j(u)|JF_j(u) ≤ ρJF_j(u). By A2a, |ω(G_j(s,u))(∂G_j(s,u))| ≤ |ω|_∞JG_j(s,u) ≤ ρ|ω|_∞JF_j(u).
F4 ((REP) for R). Since F_j(A_j) ⊆ spt S, (LF) for S with the compact set C = spt S gives Σ_j ∫_{A_j}|g_j|JF_j < ∞. So by F3 each g̃_jω(G_j)(∂G_j) is integrable on Ã_j, and Fubini applies. Use B3, (REP) for S applied to the test k-form γ := ζK_{k+1}ω, ζ(F_j(u)) = 1 (as F_j(u) ∈ spt S ⊆ V), and F3:
 R(ω) = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} g_j(u)(K_{k+1}ω)(F_j(u))(∂F_j(u)) du = Σ_j ∫_{Ã_j} g̃_j(w) ω(G_j(w))(∂G_j(w)) dw.
F5 ((LF) for R). For every compact C, Σ_j ∫_{Ã_j ∩ G_j^{-1}(C)} |g̃_j|JG_j ≤ ρΣ_j ∫_{A_j}|g_j|JF_j < ∞, by F3.
Thus (G_j, Ã_j, g̃_j) is a parametrization of R of dimension d := k + 1 = n + 2.

PART G. R is integer multiplicity.
Write the parametrization of F5 as (F_j, A_j, g_j), with F_j : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and d ≥ 2.
G1 (absolute convergence). By A2a, |g_j(u)ω(F_j u)(∂F_j u)| ≤ |ω|_∞|g_j(u)|JF_j(u)1_{F_j^{-1}(tsupport ω)}(u) for every u. So by (LF) with C = tsupport ω, the integrals and the series in (REP) converge absolutely.
G2 (good pieces).
 - Let A°_j := {u ∈ A_j ∩ G_{F_j} : g_j(u) ≠ 0} (Borel). On A_j ∖ A°_j the integrand of (REP) and the weight |g_j|JF_j vanish: either g_j = 0; or F_j is not differentiable at u, so ∂F_j(u) = 0 (as d ≥ 1); or ∂F_j(u) is linearly dependent (A2). So (REP) and (LF) hold with A_j replaced by A°_j.
 - Split every A°_j ⊆ G_{F_j} into pieces by C1, and enumerate all pairs (j, piece) as (Φ_l, P_l, h_l)_{l∈ℕ} with Φ_l := F_j and h_l := g_j·1_{P_l}. By G1 the double family of integrals is absolutely summable, so countable additivity over the pieces and rearrangement give (REP) and (LF) for (Φ_l, P_l, h_l).
 - Each Φ_l is Lipschitz, anti-Lipschitz on P_l (constant c_l > 0), and differentiable on P_l with injective derivative; moreover |h_l| ≥ 1 on P_l.
G3 (images).
 - N_l := Φ_l(P_l) is Borel and ψ_l := (Φ_l|P_l)^{-1} is Borel (C2(b)). For y ∈ N_l put ξ_l(y) := ξ_{DΦ_l(ψ_l y)} (A2b; Borel in y) and h̃_l(y) := h_l(ψ_l y) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}.
 - For compact C, H^d(N_l ∩ C) = ∫_{P_l ∩ Φ_l^{-1}C} JΦ_l ≤ ∫_{P_l ∩ Φ_l^{-1}C} |h_l|JΦ_l by C2(c). So Σ_l H^d(N_l ∩ C) < ∞, and N := ⋃_l N_l is a Borel set with H^d(N ∩ C) < ∞ for compact C.
 - On P_l, h_l(u)ω(Φ_l u)(∂Φ_l u) = h̃_l(Φ_l u) ξ_l(Φ_l u)(ω(Φ_l u)) JΦ_l(u) (A2b). So C2(c) gives ∫_{P_l} h_l ω(Φ_l)(∂Φ_l) du = ∫_{N_l} h̃_l ξ_l(ω) dH^d, hence R(ω) = Σ_l ∫_{N_l} h̃_l ξ_l(ω) dH^d.
G4 (tangent planes).
 - By Claim D for (Φ_l, Y := N), for L^d-a.e. u ∈ P_l the set N has approximate tangent space DΦ_l(u)(ℝ^d) at Φ_l(u).
 - Remove from each P_l a Borel L^d-null set containing the exceptions. By C2(e) this removes an H^d-null set from N_l and from N; it changes no integral, and by C4(b) it changes no approximate tangent space of N.
 - Now, for every l and every y ∈ N_l, N has approximate tangent space T_y := DΦ_l(ψ_l y)(ℝ^d). This is independent of l by uniqueness (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), and ξ_l(y) is a unit orientation of T_y (A2b). So by A3(a), ξ_l(y) = ±ξ_{l'}(y) whenever y ∈ N_l ∩ N_{l'}.
G5 (integer multiplicity).
 - For y ∈ N let κ(y) := min{l : y ∈ N_l} and η(y) := ξ_{κ(y)}(y). This is Borel, since {κ = l} = N_l ∖ ⋃_{l'<l}N_{l'}.
 - For y ∈ N_l let σ_l(y) ∈ {1, −1} with ξ_l(y) = σ_l(y)η(y). This is Borel: σ_l(y) = 1 iff ‖ξ_l(y) − η(y)‖ < ‖ξ_l(y) + η(y)‖.
 - For compact C, ∫_C Σ_l 1_{N_l}|h̃_l| dH^d = Σ_l ∫_{P_l ∩ Φ_l^{-1}C}|h_l|JΦ_l < ∞ (C2(c)), and every nonzero term has |h̃_l| ≥ 1. So for H^d-a.e. y only finitely many l satisfy y ∈ N_l. Let N° ⊆ N be the Borel set of such y; then H^d(N ∖ N°) = 0. On N° put m(y) := Σ_l 1_{N_l}(y)σ_l(y)h̃_l(y) ∈ ℤ.
 - Dominated convergence (dominating function |ω|_∞1_{tsupport ω}Σ_l 1_{N_l}|h̃_l| ∈ L¹(H^d), by A3(b)) gives R(ω) = ∫_{N°} m η(ω) dH^d.
 - Let M' := {y ∈ N° : m(y) ≠ 0} (Borel). Put θ'(y) := |m(y)| ∈ ℕ on M' and θ' := 0 elsewhere, and ξ'(y) := sign(m(y))η(y) on M' and ξ' := 0 elsewhere. Then R(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'ξ'(ω) dH^d for every test d-form ω.
G6 (the IMRep). (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep of dimension d in U = ℝ^P:
